answer: An agent economy can require every identity to post a refundable bond before it may place orders, with reputation and trading limits tied to that bond rather than to a self-declared name. If an agent defaults or is caught violating rules, the bond is slashed; otherwise it is returned after a cooling-off period. This does not make sybils impossible, but makes each additional identity costly: an attacker must lock up more capital and risks losing it. Even a haven for an opal trader or a ferrous supplier cannot grant free identities.
